The signal "Interface version ID {major, minor, patch}" provides the version information of the interface.

Requirement:
The signal "Interface version ID {major, minor, patch}" is assigned in the system design phase.

The signal "Interface ID" is used to uniquely identify the originated interface type of the message.

Additional information:
The enumerators may differentiate the sensor's sensor technology
The signal "Interface ID" is necessary, for example, for a service-oriented architecture.
The signal "Number of valid serving sensors" provides the number of valid sensors serving the interface.

The signal "Sensor ID" which uniquely identifies the sensor and link the data of different sensors' interface.

Additional information:
It is required to associate the logical interfaces of one sensor or a sensor cluster with its sensors.
Each signal "Sensor ID" value shall serve independently at least one interface.
The signal "Sensor ID" is necessary, for example, for a service-oriented architecture.

Requirement:
The signal's "Sensor ID" value is assigned during the system design phase.

The signal "Time stamp - measurement" provides the time stamp at which the measurement was taken (not the time at which it was processed or at which it is transmitted) in the vehicle-global synchronised time. Clock synchronisation shall be ensured, depending on bus technology.

Additional information:
The signal's "Time stamp - measurement" value shall be selected so that it is as consistent as possible with the measured entities and the associated time error is minimum. Each entity of a detection list may have, for example, the signal "Time stamp defference - detection level" for its measurement (for example, for integrating sensor technologies). In case of a continuous or a subdivided measurement cycle, the signal "Time stamp difference - detection level" shall be used to differentiate the real measured point in time of the entity acquisition.
Time stamps are consistent for all vehicle electronic control units(ECUs).

The signal "Cycle counter" provides the continuous up counter to identify the message cycle of ther interface
It counts up per every cycle of a complete prediction, tracking or a single measurement.

Additional information:
This information can be determined from signal's "Time stamp - <...>" value and the sensor's cycle period [see the signal "Interface cycle time" and "Interface cycle time - variation"].
Each sensor as well as each sensor cluster uses a local sensor cycle counter per interface.

The signal "Interface cycle time" provides the representative cycle time of the interface's messages.
Normally, each interface sends the complete interface message cyclically. The period between two messages can vary. Each interface header defines the interface's cycle time and the variation of the cycle time [see signal "Interface cycle time - variation"].

Additional information:
If the signal "Interface cycle time - variation" is 100%, the message is sent in the case one or several signals have changed their value.

The signal "Interface cycle time - variation" provides the possible variation of the expected representative cycle time [see signal "Interface cycle time"] of the interface's messages.

Additional information:
If the signal "Interface cycle time - variation" is 100%, the message is sent in the case one or several signals have changed their value, for example, the possible, allowed cycle time for the next cycle: 0 s ? next cycle time ? infinity s. This may indicate that the next cycle is triggered by an event.

Example:
The duration between two sequentially sent messages of an interface is in the range [interface cycle time x (1 - interface cycle time variation / 100%), interface cycle time / ( 1 - interface cycle time variation / 100%)].
The signal "Data qualifier" expresses whether the content of the entity list of the interface can be used or not. It can change dynamically over time and inform about temporal restrictions.

column3: The signal "Radial velocity ambiguity domain {begin, end}" provides a description of the Doppler ambiguity caused by under-sampling.

The range of the ambiguity domain is defined by {begin} and {end}.
The defined range is only one possible solution for an ambiguous measurement method (for example, under-sampling).
The azimuth angle of the ambiguity domain is defined by {begin} and {end}. The defined azimuth angle is only one possible solution for an ambiguous measurement method.
The elevation angle of the ambiguity domain is defined by {begin} and {end}. The defined elevation angle is only one possible solution for an ambiguous measurement method.

The signal "Recognised detections - capability" provides the performance of the sensor cluster's interface. It determines how many entities the sensor cluster is guaranteed to recognise, for example, at full load with respect to the current scenario.
The signal "Recognised detections - status" determines whether the sensor cluster's interface can process all recognised entities or whether it works at the sensor cluster's performance limits.

column3:
The signal's "Number of valid detections" value defines the number of valid entities in the detection list of a DLI.
One measurement can generate more than one similar detection, if there are ambiguities.

Additional information:
The entries in the list may or may not be sorted.
All those entities of the list which can be used by the fusion unit are regarded as valid.
The list includes a complete and prioritised set of valid entities for the signal's "Time stamp - <...>" value and not only differential list between two sequential time stamps.
